phpstan-assert-functions.scope: arrayHasNumericKey, arrayHasStringKey, arrayHasExprKey; not the extension implementation

psalm-testcase.scope: setUp, Before, provider row shape, required/default/variadic arguments; legacy examples are not modern PHPUnit contracts

phpunit-array-key.scope: PHPUnit 12.5.0; string/integer keys, ArrayAccess, success and failure datasets

phpunit-assertions.scope: assertArrayHasKey, assertArrayNotHasKey, assertSame, assertEquals; versioned but mutable documentation

phpunit-providers.scope: public static iterable-of-arrays; provider execution before setup; versioned but mutable documentation

mago-2383.scope: historical native Mago gap, not evidence of a gap in this extension

cases.title: Literal method assertion establishes key presence
cases.fixture: <?php use PHPUnit\Framework\Assert; /** @param array{k?: string} $a */ function check(array $a): string { Assert::assertArrayHasKey('k', $a); return $a['k']; }
cases.semantics: On normal return the literal key exists. Other optional keys remain optional.
cases.analyzer_expectation: No undefined-key diagnostic on the asserted offset. Preserve diagnostics on an unrelated offset.
cases.negative_control: Assert 'k', then read optional 'other'; also remove the assertion.
cases.versions: Mago 1.58.2 conformance verified across PHPUnit 10.5.66, 11.5.57, 12.5.42 and 13.4.5. Exact PHP combinations are recorded in cycles/001-A003.md.

cases.title: Key presence does not imply a non-null value
cases.semantics: A null-valued array entry is present. HasKey must not become HasNonnullEntryForKey.
cases.analyzer_expectation: After the assertion, returning the nullable entry from a string-returning function remains invalid.
cases.negative_control: assertArrayNotHasKey('k', ['k' => null]) must fail. A nullable-return diagnostic must survive narrowing.
cases.versions: Function conformance and runtime checked across the cycle 001 matrix. Non-null mutation killed. A separate nullable method-call fixture remains untested.

cases.title: Namespaced assertion function establishes key presence
cases.fixture: <?php use function PHPUnit\Framework\assertArrayHasKey; /** @param array{k?: string|null} $a */ function check(array $a): string|null { assertArrayHasKey('k', $a); return $a['k']; }
cases.semantics: The public namespaced assertion function has the same key-existence postcondition as the method.
cases.analyzer_expectation: Narrow the asserted key on normal return. PHPStan's hasOffset spelling is analyzer-specific and is not required.
cases.negative_control: Unasserted, other-key, variable-key and unrelated-function reads retain four offset warnings. Nullable returns retain both errors. Disabling extensions restores seven string-offset and one integer-offset warnings. Reordered named arguments retain two native no-named-arguments diagnostics.
cases.versions: Red before fix on PHPUnit 12.5.40 / Mago 1.58.2; green across cycle 001's seven PHP/PHPUnit combinations. PHPStan fixture is pinned; PHPStan itself was not executed. Named argument names are not a PHPUnit compatibility guarantee.

cases.title: Canonical numeric string keys alias integer keys
cases.semantics: PHP array key conversion makes '7' and 7 equivalent. '07' remains a distinct string key.
cases.analyzer_expectation: Preserve PHP key normalization, without treating every numeric-looking string as an integer.
cases.versions: Runtime checked on 11.5.0 and 12.5.0; no claim about all PHP numeric string edge cases.

cases.title: ArrayAccess remains an object
cases.semantics: ArrayAccess is accepted, but the assertion must not turn the object into an array. User-defined offsetExists need not prove offsetGet is non-null.
cases.analyzer_expectation: Keep object identity and do not infer an array shape on ArrayAccess.
cases.negative_control: A missing offset fails; retain methods of the ArrayAccess implementation after assertion.
cases.versions: ArrayObject runtime checked on 11.5.0 and 12.5.0. Arbitrary ArrayAccess side effects remain untested.

cases.title: Equality must not become identity narrowing
cases.semantics: The equality assertion passes; the identity assertion fails because the types differ.
cases.analyzer_expectation: Do not narrow an actual string to integer merely because assertEquals used an integer expected value.
cases.negative_control: The assertSame call must fail at runtime, while assertEquals passes.
cases.versions: Runtime checked on 11.5.0 and 12.5.0. Native assertSame coverage exists but does not establish assertEquals conformance.

cases.title: Providers yield arrays with required test arguments
cases.fixture: <?php use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase; use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\DataProvider; final class RowsTest extends TestCase { public static function rows(): iterable { yield [7]; } #[DataProvider('rows')] public function testRow(int $n, string $suffix = '', int ...$rest): void { self::assertSame(7, $n); } }
cases.semantics: A provider returns iterable rows; each row is an array. Default and variadic parameters may be omitted, required parameters may not.
cases.analyzer_expectation: Report required-argument and concrete type mismatches. Psalm issue names and its handling of untyped providers are not PHPUnit requirements.
cases.negative_control: Remove the default from suffix, or yield scalar 7 instead of [7].
cases.versions: Modern fixture uses public static and attributes. Psalm's non-static annotation examples must not be copied into PHPUnit 12+ fixtures.

cases.title: Providers execute before lifecycle initialization
cases.fixture: <?php use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase; use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\DataProvider; final class OrderTest extends TestCase { private static bool $ready = false; public static function setUpBeforeClass(): void { self::$ready = true; } public static function rows(): array { return [[self::$ready]]; } #[DataProvider('rows')] public function testOrder(bool $ready): void { self::assertFalse($ready); } }
cases.semantics: Providers run before setUpBeforeClass and before the first setUp. Initialization knowledge cannot flow backwards into providers.
cases.analyzer_expectation: Do not assume test lifecycle initialization in data provider bodies.
cases.negative_control: Change the expectation to assertTrue; the runtime test must fail.
cases.versions: Documented for PHPUnit 12.5. Runtime and Mago checks pending.

cases.title: TestCase setup initializes test properties
cases.fixture: <?php use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase; final class SetupTest extends TestCase { private string $value; protected function setUp(): void { $this->value = 'ready'; } public function testValue(): void { self::assertSame('ready', $this->value); } }
cases.semantics: TestCase setup runs before a test. An unrelated class's method called setUp has no PHPUnit lifecycle meaning.
cases.analyzer_expectation: Accept unconditional setup assignment, including inherited setup. Do not suppress missing initialization merely because setUp exists.
cases.negative_control: Remove the assignment, or remove TestCase inheritance.
cases.versions: Existing suite green across cycle 001's seven combinations on Mago 1.58.2. Conditional assignments remain an explicitly documented Mago limitation.
